# Cross-source inference from OULAD to a MOOC first-event task

After the two fixed-queue rules were scored, test transport of a previously fitted FL model to the independent MOOC trace. This is an exploratory mechanism check. Keep the midpoint, roster and observed first-event label from the external queue protocol. Day-level proxies map click count to observed action count, active days to distinct floor(timestamp/86400), recency to decision day minus last active day, and visited sites to distinct activity IDs. Apply the archived log1p/4 transform in source feature order. No target labels or target-fitted preprocessing enter scoring. The source window was 61 days and the destination provides roughly 15 at the midpoint. Compare AUROC primarily, and Brier descriptively. Retain the original .02 AUC threshold and simultaneous positive lower bound as a diagnostic. A single receiving stream does not give a macro-institution estimand.

Use published numeric coefficients for federated Newton and matched pooled Newton. Recover the previously fitted source linear equations for FedAvg, FedProx, pooled gradient descent, and all seven per-module local, intercept-only, weak-ridge and adapted equations by solving against exported source logits and source design rows, without labels. Check matrix rank and reproduce every archived probability to within 1e-9, or stop. With no receiving module label, publish each per-module transfer and the prespecified equal-weight mean of predicted probabilities across modules for each local family. Include both directions of recency and count, previously scored on the destination. Compare Newton against all available score rules with simultaneous two-sided Bonferroni paired DeLong intervals. Tied ranks get half credit. Omit Brier for ordering-only controls with no probability forecast. Neural and tree weights are unavailable in the archived forecasts; they cannot be reconstructed using an assumed linear model. Preserve this limitation. No target-side client training, privacy or cross-university FL claim.
